Definition: of uncertain affinity; to sob, i.e. wail aloud (whereas 1145 is rather to cry silently):--bewail, weep.
KeyPassages: Matthew 2:18; Mark 5:38; Luke 6:21; John 11:31; Acts 9:39; Romans 12:15
BiblicalUsage: Klaio means to weep aloud, to sob and wail. Matthew 2:18 hears Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted, Mark 5:38 shows the house in tumult with them that wept and wailed greatly, and John 11:31 follows Mary to the grave to weep there. Luke 6:21 promises, blessed are ye that weep now, for ye shall laugh, Acts 9:39 has the widows standing by Peter weeping and showing the coats Dorcas made, and Romans 12:15 commands, weep with them that weep.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Bible never tells the weeping to stop: Rachel weeps, Mary weeps, the widows weep, and the promise is not that tears are wrong but that they will turn to laughter. I hold that Romans 12:15 is the whole ministry of tears in one line, that we weep with them that weep because Christ wept with us first.
RelatedBooks: Matthew; Mark; Luke; John; Acts; Romans
